Exact proof identifies full domain and forbids extrapolation beyond n=11.

originality.rationale: Four relevant full-text primary works were compared for implication of common shortest reset thresholds: classical shortest individual reset words, single-automaton BFS, language intersection via product, random pair-of-states coalescence, and census experiments. None of their examined claims contains or implies the specific 45-entry pair spectrum without further finite computation. The original product identity and single-size results are expressly excluded from novelty; an unindexed exact enumeration remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact enumeration of shortest common reset words for the Černý pair family may exist; full-text coverage cannot exclude all historical sources.
The numerically observed finite maximum-overhead pattern might hold beyond n=11, but no such general theorem is claimed.

value.rationale: Exact complete natural 45-case classification of simultaneous two-device reset latency, a resource distinct from single-system Černý thresholds. The finite sharp overhead maximum is \(n-3\) for each \(3\le n\le11\); nonmonotone smaller-partner dependence and a provable arithmetic zero-overhead baseline are useful design distinctions; no general formula is alleged.
